q: Which statement about the least-squares cost for linear regression is true?
opts: It can have several local minima
It is convex, so any local minimum is global
It is only convex after feature scaling
why: J is a convex quadratic in θ (Hessian XᵀX/n is PSD).

wrong.0: That happens for neural networks, not for least squares.
wrong.2: Scaling changes the shape (conditioning), not convexity.

q: Points (1,1), (2,2), (3,3), θ₀ = 0, θ₁ = 0.5. Compute J(θ₁) = 1/(2n) Σ(h−y)². Round to 2 decimals.
x = [1,2,3,4,5], y = [2,3,4,5,6]. Using the normal equation, what is θ₁ (the slope)?
Which are valid fixes when XᵀX is not invertible? (Select all)
why: pinv and removing dependent features are on p.34; Ridge makes the matrix invertible.

wrong.2: The normal equation has no learning rate.

q: In gradient descent you should update θ₀ first and then use the new θ₀ when computing θ₁'s update.
why: Updates must be simultaneous: compute all gradients from the old θ, then update.

q: CHD example (p.52): w₀ = 5, w₁ = w₂ = −0.03, α = 0.02, n = 3, Σ(ŷ−y) = −0.24. What is the new w₀? (4 decimals)
Your batch GD cost increases every iteration. Most likely cause?
why: A too-large α overshoots and diverges.

wrong.0: Too small gives slow but steady decrease.

q: Which variant updates parameters after every single training example?
why: SGD computes the derivative from one instance and updates immediately.

q: y = w₀ + w₁x + w₂x² is a linear model.
why: It is linear in the weights w.
More data, early stopping and regularisation all reduce variance.

q: Which regulariser can set coefficients exactly to zero?

wrong.0: L2 shrinks weights but rarely makes them exactly 0.

q: In the slide's Elastic Net formula, r = 1 gives…
why: r multiplies the L2 term in the slide's formula, so r = 1 is Ridge. (scikit-learn's l1_ratio = 1 would be Lasso.)
